text: In Madrid, a senior Abwehr officer, Karl-Erich Kühlenthal, asked Admiral Wilhelm Canaris, the head of German military intelligence, to intervene. The Spanish found a way to read the letters without breaking the seals. They wound the damp paper tightly around a thin probe and drew it out through the gap beneath the envelope flap. The letters were dried, photographed, soaked in salt water again, and put back.
